findings.title: Invalid ERB Ruby prevents existing discussions from rendering
findings.body: The conditional is closed with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby because the trailing `if` has no condition. Rails will raise a template syntax error whenever an existing embedded topic renders this view, so the discussion iframe returns an error instead of showing comments. Close the block with `end`.

findings.title: Imported feed HTML bypasses sanitization
findings.body: Imported contents are stored with the `raw_html` cook method, whose implementation returns the raw text without sanitizing it. `absolutize_urls` only parses and rewrites URLs; it does not remove scripts, event-handler attributes, or dangerous link schemes. The RSS polling path passes feed contents directly into this method, so executable HTML from a feed is persisted as cooked content and rendered on the forum's origin. Sanitize imported HTML before storing it, including on updates.

findings.title: RSS entries without a content element abort feed polling
findings.body: The poller assumes every entry has a non-nil `content` value and calls `scrub` on it. Ordinary RSS entries can provide their body in `description` rather than an Atom-style `content` element, and entries may omit a body entirely. Such an entry raises an exception and stops the entire polling run, preventing subsequent entries from being imported. Support the RSS body fields and handle missing content explicitly.

findings.title: Remote retrieval follows redirects outside the allowed host
findings.body: TopicRetriever checks only the host of the initial embed URL, but `open(url).read` follows HTTP redirects without checking their destinations. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host, including an internal HTTP service, therefore bypasses the embedding host restriction and can have its response imported into a public topic. Validate every redirect destination and restrict retrieval to permitted HTTP(S) endpoints before fetching it.

findings.title: URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths
findings.body: The rewrite treats every URL beginning with `/` as a path on the article's host. For example, `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` becomes `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`; the image rewrite below has the same problem. Conversely, document-relative URLs such as `images/photo.jpg` are left unchanged and resolve against the Discourse URL rather than the source article. This breaks links and images in imported articles. Resolve URLs against the complete source URL using URI joining, preserving protocol-relative hosts.
